The target is a contract that is both correct and executable without creating decision.jsonl. A signal is a skill gap when the interview should have resolved it through an owner question, repository discovery, an explicit approved default, or an explicit delegation boundary. Technical choices count when another reasonable choice changes observable behavior, compatibility, safety, cost, data, acceptance, or reversibility. Apply the supplied strategy as exactly one bounded edit to the baseline skill. The anchor_exact_text must be copied verbatim from one unique baseline passage. For replace, provide its replacement; for delete, replacement_text must be empty; for add, provide text inserted immediately after the anchor. Anchor and replacement are each limited to 120 words. Do not add repository-specific names or solutions. Absence of evidence for broader behavior does not authorize narrower behavior, exclusions, preservation guarantees, or implementation boundaries. Include exactly one signal_reviews item for every input signal and list every skill-gap signal ID in addressed_signal_ids that this single edit directly addresses.
Return only the JSON required by the supplied schema.

# Interview

Inspect the request and repository.
Ask only questions whose answers can materially change the resulting contract.
Produce the runtime-required contract without inventing unauthorized behavior.

This is diagnostic rather than an issue-time recall failure, but implementing the sealed check would reject the audited successful behavior.

The specified split_surds fallback returns (S.One, S.Zero, expr), which _sqrt_match converts to the truthy list [expr, S.Zero, S.One]. The audited control flow only returns the original square root when _sqrt_match produces no match, so the contract's claim that this fallback makes matching decline is unsupported and may alter downstream denesting behavior.

Changing event dispatch from the existing single formatted-signature path to one event invocation per overload could alter extension-handler call counts and output semantics without audited compatibility evidence.

Treating every consecutive accepted signature as an overload without a continuation marker differs from the hindsight-observed implementation, which required a trailing backslash to continue collection; diagnostically, the contract could consume adjacent signature-looking content that the gold behavior preserves.
Invoke autodoc-process-signature independently for every extracted overload; neither the public request nor audited repository facts establish this behavior.
Require disabled-mode, explicit-signature, late-signature, event-transformation, and event-suppression coverage beyond the narrowly requested overload behavior and existing regression expectations.
Stopping the entire leading-block scan on a syntactically valid but non-accepted name may differ from existing candidate-search behavior and was not established by repository evidence.
Require a non-accepted leading signature to terminate extraction and preserve all following content; this extrapolates beyond the owner's answered scan-boundary decision.
Require documentation changes; sensible, but not stated by the requester or necessary to define the requested behavior.
Support per-overload suppression through autodoc-process-signature, despite the event return contract being explicitly unaudited.
